title: TRADE REQUEST Looking for JS programmer/co-developer

posts.author: SolisValoris
posts.body:
DISCLAIMER: Game contains topics not suitable for a younger audience like graphic violence, disturbing imagery, sexual references and harsh language.
Hello! We're an international team of 15, based in Spain. Most of us artists, voice actors and musicians.
We have two developers, me and a professional programmer but he's not very acquaintanced with RPGmaker yet, we need a companion with RPGmaker MV and some knowledge on it to aid us with our project: "Taste of Terror".
It is a story-driven musical psychological horror sci-fa RPG.
Some of the mechanics it features are:
- Strategic (rock-paper-scissor style) turn-based battle system
- Complex branching
- Animated musical cutscenes
- Fusion. Characters can fuse with others creating new ones.
- Relationship levels. The game's most important theme is relationship dynamics, the exploration of healthy and toxic friendships or family relationships. So this is important and tied to the complex branching of the game.
-
Canping.
Mechanic used in older RPGs that has been lost throughout the years, with a twist. Camping in a can... They're food, this way they won't expire. In this can they can improve their relationship levels, save the game, etc.
We've developed so far a demo which is not posted publicly yet, but we've showcased it publicly before.
The game tells the story of Noah, the hero of the game, who finds themselves trapped in Savoria, a surreal and mysterious world where struggling spirits are sent—and where everyone takes on the form of food. In this strange and perilous land, Noah has formed strong bonds with characters like Pat and others they encounters along the way. Together, they navigate the challenges of survival in a world where even friendship can be fleeting.
Your goal is to explore the vibrant yet haunting realm of Savoria, uncover the secrets of why you—and others—are here, and confront the truth behind its existence. All the while, you must fight against an ominous threat: as food, you have an expiration date. To stay alive, you'll need to discover innovative methods to stave off your inevitable decay and forge a path toward survival.
The story delves deeply into several powerful themes:
Relationships: The game explores the intricacies of human connections—not just romantic relationships, but the bonds between friends, family, and even unlikely allies. These relationships play a central role in shaping the characters and driving the narrative forward.
Mythology and the Stars: Drawing inspiration from the stars and space, the game takes inspiration from mythological elements tied to celestial phenomena. The narrative is underpinned by rigorous research, often in collaboration with subject matter experts, to ensure an authentic portrayal.
Social Issues: At its core, the game uses its fantastical setting to highlight real-world social issues, offering thoughtful commentary on topics like inequality, trauma, and the human condition.
Mortality and Survival: The constant presence of an expiration date serves as a metaphor for life's impermanence, forcing players to confront their own mortality while exploring the lengths one might go to survive.
Identity and Transformation: Characters grapple with their sense of self in a world that reduces them to literal personified food items. The game explores how external labels and roles shape identity and how individuals can transcend those limitations.
Sacrifice and Selflessness: Many challenges in the game require choices that test the player’s willingness to sacrifice for others, whether it’s for friendship, love, or the greater good of Savoria.
Trauma and Healing: Each character’s journey reflects real-world struggles with trauma, emphasizing the importance of understanding, resilience, and finding ways to heal—even in the face of overwhelming odds.
Justice and Corruption: The societal structure of Savoria raises questions about fairness, power, and the ways systems can fail those they are meant to protect. The game critiques authority figures through its allegorical storytelling.
Cultural and Personal Legacy: The game delves into what it means to leave a mark, whether through personal connections, actions, or the traditions passed down through generations. This ties into Savoria’s rich mythological backstory.
Unity and Division: The fragmented factions of Savoria represent both the beauty of diversity and the dangers of division, challenging players to bridge gaps and foster understanding between wildly different ideologies and cultures.
These themes intertwine to create a layered and emotionally resonant story, where every decision, song, and battle invites players to reflect on the complexities of life, love, and loss.
We mainly need help building the base game and mechanics, such as the battle system, GUI, menu, accessibility, etc...
This game's team, Solis Valoris, has been invited to devcom, gamescom and DevGAMM before, even gotten its own panel in New Gaming, and we also have some very important people on the team, so all I ask is for someone who will be serious and loyal (loyal as in, don't tell anyone and especially not publicly about the game's storyline, endings, spoilers, the team's plans for the future, etc.) about this.
In return I can offer the following, for the same value of your work:
- Spanish is my first language, I have a bilingual English and I have studied translation and interpreting in University, with a specialty in audio-visual. I can translate from Spanish to English and vice-versa.
- I'm a professional artist with 5 years experience having worked in different projects. But I got my degree 7 years ago. My specialty is 2d art, concept art and illustration, but I can also animate.
- I make merch: resin keychains/pins, holographic stickers, earrings, charms, etc. And I have 2 years of experience going to artist alleys almost weekly
You may message me for proof for what I have said, some info about the game and examples of my work, setups from past exhibitions, our pitches, my CV and anything else you may need.

The battle system as in the math, for calculating attacks, damage, etc... I'm really not good at math. My aforementioned teammate is, but he doesn't know very well how to use the RPG maker engine.
I think if there's good communication we can all work together.
For the GUI and accessibility it's basically to make a customized UI that works. Currently I'm using the preset one, with a custom window and that's it. This is because the preset UI doesn't align with the game's theme and aesthetic.
Its already designed we'd just have to make it work.
As for accessibility, I would like for the game to be as accessible as possible, and be able to add things in the menu like language change, font change for readability, etc.
I do all the eventing and mapping. It is mostly customising & building the base game that's giving me a huge headache.
I hope this answers your doubts and thanks for the interest!
Cheers!
